holidays.name: National Relaxation Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to doing absolutely nothing productive. Put down the to-do list, silence your phone, and give yourself official permission to lounge around guilt-free.
holidays.origin: Founded in 1985 by Colleen Paige, a children's lifestyle and family expert, who also created National Wiggle Your Toes Day and National Dog Day.
holidays.funFact: It falls near the end of summer, when many people are squeezing in their last vacations, which makes it a perfect excuse to nap in a hammock.

holidays.name: National Lemon Meringue Pie Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the tart, sweet, cloud-topped dessert with a golden toasted meringue. Bakers and pie fans celebrate with slices of this tangy classic.
holidays.origin: A food holiday that grew out of American pie-appreciation traditions. Lemon meringue pie rose to popularity in the 19th century, thanks in part to cookbook author Elizabeth Coane Goodfellow of Philadelphia, who is often credited with perfecting the recipe.
holidays.funFact: The meringue topping can weep, forming little beads of moisture, and pastry chefs have a whole arsenal of tricks to prevent it.

holidays.name: National Failure Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace your flops, blunders, and faceplants as stepping stones to success. Celebrants share their most spectacular failures and what they learned from them.
holidays.origin: An informal observance on August 15 that encourages people to reframe failure as a learning tool, echoing the popular idea that great successes are built on many failed attempts.
holidays.funFact: James Dyson reportedly made 5,126 prototypes of his bagless vacuum cleaner before he got one that worked.

holidays.name: Assumption of Mary Feast Day with Herb Blessing
holidays.description: In many European countries, people bring bundles of herbs, flowers, and grains to church to be blessed on this day. The bundles are then hung in homes for protection and healing.
holidays.origin: Rooted in Christian tradition celebrating the Assumption of Mary, combined with older harvest customs. In Germany it is known as Kräuterweihe or Mariä Himmelfahrt.
holidays.funFact: In Germany these bundles, called Kräuterbuschen, traditionally contain seven, nine, or even 99 different herbs and flowers, depending on the region.

holidays.name: National Check the Chip Day
holidays.description: A day reminding people to check that their pet's microchip information is current. It is a practical and heartwarming way to help lost pets find their way home.
holidays.origin: Created by the American Veterinary Medical Association and pet-industry partners to promote microchip registration and updates, and it falls on August 15 each year.
holidays.funFact: Many microchips are about the size of a grain of rice, but they only work if the owner's contact details are registered and up to date.
